paragraphs.text: In answer to my prayer he replied, Thou hast well prayed, sed stat sententia, I am set, I am inexorable.
paragraphs.anchor: Then said the Lord unto me.

paragraphs.text: That chancellor of heaven, as one calleth him; who not only "ruled with God," but overruled. {Exo 32:11-14,Num 14:19-20}
paragraphs.anchor: Though Moses.

paragraphs.text: A mighty man likewise in prayer. See 1Sa 7:9, called therefore Pethuel, as some think, {Joe 1:1} that is, a God persuader. These two were famous in their generations for hearty love to, and prayers for, that rebellious people, and did much for them. But, so the case now stood, if these favourites were alive, and should intercede their utmost for them, it should avail nothing. See Eze 14:14.
paragraphs.anchor: And Samuel.

paragraphs.text: This is spoken after the manner of men - q.d., I am implacably enraged, I am unchangeably resolved against them.
paragraphs.anchor: Yet my mind could not be to this people.

paragraphs.text: Tell them that I have utterly rejected them, and I will ratify and realise thy speeches. See on Jer 1:10.
paragraphs.anchor: Cast them out of my sight.

paragraphs.text: Or, Let them be gone - q.d., I am the worse to look upon them.
paragraphs.anchor: And let them go forth.

paragraphs.text: As they will be apt enough to do in a jeer.
paragraphs.anchor: If they say unto thee.

paragraphs.text: i.e., For the pestilence commonly called mortality, because it is so deadly a disease. Those at Genoa have lately found it so. And yet it is here reckoned first, as the least and tightest of all the four threatened judgments, which must needs be bad enough when the pest is the best of them all. The Turks shun not the company of those that have the plague, but pointing upon their foreheads, say it was written there at their birth when they should die, and of what disease. These in the text could as little avoid the deaths they were assigned to, as Aeschylus the tragedian could his being knocked on the head. For whenas he was foretold that he should die with a stroke coming from above, he shunned houses, and was wont to remain in the open air, but he was killed by a tortoise falling from the mouth of an eagle upon his bald head, mistaken for a stone. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Such as are for death

paragraphs.text: {a} Aelian, l. 1. c. 5. s. 19. 1:225,227; Valerius Maximus, l. 9. ext. c. 12. 1:375
Heb., Families, or kindreds - i.e., quatuor cognata carnivora, dogs, birds, and beasts being added to the former four evils, {Jer 15:2} quasi per auxesin.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will appoint over them four kinds.

paragraphs.text: Because of his sins, idolatry and bloodshed especially, wherein the people partook and persisted, and were therefore justly punished.
paragraphs.anchor: Because of Manasseh.

paragraphs.text: But altogether degenerate. He was therefore the worse, because he should have been better, and yet the worse again, because he was author publicae corruptelae, a ringleader of rebellion to others, as was Jeroboam.
paragraphs.anchor: The son of Hezekiah.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Who shall come out of his place to comfort thee? Or, Who shall shake his head in commiseration to thee?
paragraphs.anchor: Who shall bemoan thee?

paragraphs.text: Patiendo, ac parcendo. I have so oft revoked my threats, that unless I should wrong my justice, I can do so no more.
paragraphs.anchor: I am weary with repenting.

paragraphs.text: Not of purgation {a} {as Jer 6:29-30} but of perdition. Such as that, Jer 51:2.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will fan them with a fan.

paragraphs.text: As men use to winnow grain at a windy door, where the chaff is blown quite away.
paragraphs.anchor: In the gates of the land.

paragraphs.text: {a} Deo gratias quod lingua Petiliani non sit ventilabrum Christi. - Jerome.
Or, Before me; or, In my sight.
paragraphs.anchor: The widows are increased to me.

paragraphs.text: Hyperbole.
paragraphs.anchor: Above the sands of the seas.

paragraphs.text: Nebuchadnezzar, that choice young man; for so some render the text. And so he was, when he came against Jerusalem and burned it, viz., in the eighteenth year of his reign.
paragraphs.anchor: A spoiler at noon day.

paragraphs.text: Or, Terrors, even the city; that is, say the Septuagint and Chaldee, the army of the Chaldees, which for their numbers and order of pitching their tents, seemed to be a city.
paragraphs.anchor: And terrors upon the city.

paragraphs.text: Jerusalem, that mater multipara, a fruitful mother.
paragraphs.anchor: She that hath born seven languisheth.

paragraphs.text: Heb., She putteth out her soul. {as Job 11:20} We read of some mothers who, hearing of their sons to be slain in battle, have fallen down dead in the place.
paragraphs.anchor: She hath given up the ghost.

paragraphs.text: See on Amo 8:9. A Christian, when at worst, can sing, Non omnium dierum sol occidit, Not on all days the sun sets. I look for better days yet.
paragraphs.anchor: Her sun is gone down.

paragraphs.text: scil., In such an age wherein I may not pray for my people, nor can preach unto them to any good purpose. Buchanan bewailed it that he was born nec coelo, nec solo, nec coeculo erudite. {a} Jeremiah lamenteth here for a worse matter. Surely he might well say for his manifold sufferings:
paragraphs.anchor: Woe is me, my mother, that thou hast born me

paragraphs.text: “ Littora quot conchas, quot amaens rosaria flores,
Quotque soporiferum grana papaver habet;
premor salversis, ”& c.
- Ovid., Trist.

{b} Generally opposed and quarrelled, for my free and faithful discharge of my duty. This is the world’s wages to godly ministers, whom they usually make their buttmark. But God be thanked, saith he with Jerome, quod dignus sim quem mundus oderit, that I am worthy whom the world should hate. Lutherus pascitur convitiis, saith he of himself, Luther is fed with reproaches.
paragraphs.anchor: A man of strife and a man of contention.

paragraphs.text: i.e., I have neither bought nor sold, as we say, meddled nor made with them. I have had as little to do with them any way as was possible. Usura praecipuum fomentum litium. Usuary particularily starts quarrels. I have kept myself close to my calling, and yet I cannot avoid their variance and virulencies. To preach is to derive upon a man’s self the hatred of the world, saith Luther.
paragraphs.anchor: I have neither lent on usury

paragraphs.text: {a} Camden’s Elisabeth.
{b} Virum arguentem. - Arab.
Heb., If it be not well, q.d., then trust me no more; thy latter end shall be comfortable; {Psa 37:37} the end of that man is peace, be his beginning and middle never so troublesome.
paragraphs.anchor: Verily it shall be well with thy remnant.

paragraphs.text: Or, I will intercede for thee with the enemy. See this fulfilled, Jer 40:4. God can speak for his in the hearts of their enemies, and make their foes to favour them, as many of the Papists here did Wycliffe, and after him Bradford.
paragraphs.anchor: Verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well.

paragraphs.text: That is, say some, shall these hardhearted Jews be too hard for me? or, for thee, Jeremiah, whom I have made an "iron pillar and brazen walls" against the whole land {Jer 1:18} Never think it. Brighten thee they may, but not break thee. The northern iron is noted for the best and toughest.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall iron break the northern iron and the steel?

paragraphs.text: This is spoken by an apostrophe to the people, who are here told again what to trust to for their national sins.
paragraphs.anchor: Thy substance and thy treasure.

paragraphs.text: Or, To serve thine enemies; for there is a double reading of the text.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will make thee to pass with thine enemies.

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah had begun a complaint, {Jer 15:10} not without some tang and tincture of human infirmity. Invalidum omne natura querulum. God graciously interrupted him, and came leaping over all those "mountains of Bether," all lets and impediments, to his comfort and best satisfaction. {Jer 15:11-12} Nevertheless Jeremiah hath not done, but goeth on as before; et humanum aliquid patitur.
paragraphs.anchor: O Lord, thou knowest.

paragraphs.text: He was full, and speaks thick.
paragraphs.anchor: Remember me, and visit me.

paragraphs.text: While thou bearest with them, take care of me, that I perish not by their perfidy aud cruelty.
paragraphs.anchor: Take me not away in thy longsuffering.

paragraphs.text: Ceu dabitorem compellat Deum, suaque adducit merita. He delivers himself as if he held God to be his debtor. This was not so well.
paragraphs.anchor: Know that for thy cause I have suffered rebuke.

paragraphs.text: I was well apaid of thy messages that came at first to me, and of that commission thou gavest me to be a prophet; yea, I took no small delight and complacence therein; and having found this honey, I ate it; {as Pro 25:16} but since I have met with much bitterness in this wicked world for my plain dealing. See Eze 3:3 Rev 10:10. Herodotus writeth of the river Hypanis, that for five days’ journey the water of it runneth clear and sweet; and then, for four days’ journey farther, bitter and brackish. The ministry is an honourable and comfortable function, but hath its troubles and encumbrances.
paragraphs.anchor: Thy words were found, and I did eat them.

paragraphs.text: That scoffed and mocked at God’s messages and menaces. Or, I have not sat in the assembly of those that make merry; sed serius fui, spiransque compunctionem; I came not at feasts and merry meetings since I became a prophet.
paragraphs.anchor: I sat not in the assembly of the mockers.

paragraphs.text: As Moses in like case did. {Exo 33:7}
paragraphs.anchor: I sat alone.

paragraphs.text: Here the prophet too freely expostulates with God, as less faithful, or less mindful at least, of the promised preservation. This was in a fit of diffidence and discontent, as the best have their outbursts, and the greatest lamps have needed snuffers. The Milesians, saith the philosopher, are not fools; yet they do the things that fools use to do. So the saints do oft as wicked ones, but not in the same manner and degree.
paragraphs.anchor: Why is my pain perpetual? &c.

paragraphs.text: Or, Notwithstanding, man’s perverseness breaketh not off the course of God’s goodness.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore, thus saith the Lord.

paragraphs.text: If thou cast out this devil of discontent, and (accounting distrust worse than distress) apply thyself cheerfully and constantly to the work of the ministry, I will continue and confirm thee in thine office, notwithstanding thy present frailties and failings. {a} So our Saviour, presently upon their repentance for their shameful forsaking him at his apprehension, restored his disciples to their apostolic function. {Joh 20:21-23}
paragraphs.anchor: If thou return.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The gracious from the vicious, preaching comfort to those and terror to these; not giving, as he in the fable did, straw to the dog and a bone to the ass, but to every one his proper portion, without fear or flattery. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: And if thou take forth the precious from the vile

paragraphs.text: Speaking as a prophet of mine, and as I myself would do, if in thy place.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shall be as my mouth.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Conform to thee, but do not thou chime in with them, as the false prophets do.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them return to thee

paragraphs.text: {a} Hic vides non praescribi gratiae Dei menses et annos.
{b} Probe vir, hae nihil ad te, dixit Zwinglius cum in vitia acriter inveheretur.
See on Jer 1:18-19.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will make thee.

paragraphs.text: I will, I will; never fear it, man, but go on courageously. Deal courageously, and God shall be with the good. {2Ch 19:11}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will deliver thee.
